elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause limits audits to once per calendar year, which could permit audits in consecutive months across a year-end and therefore twice within a 12-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Only 15 days' prior written notice is required.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Audits must be exercised through the F&ASC, but the clause does not require an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality obligation for the auditor or F&ASC is stated.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no off-site audit requirement or preference.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: For a Vendor-requested audit of Customer, Vendor is the requesting Party and must reimburse Customer's entire reasonable compliance costs; no underpayment-based cost shift is imposed, which is more protective than the stated 5 percent threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause does not prohibit direct access to Customer systems.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The added language limits review or audit rights against any Party to no more than once in any calendar year.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The added language requires at least 15 days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: For a Vendor-requested audit of Customer, Vendor is the requesting Party and must reimburse Customer's entire reasonable compliance costs; no underpayment-based cost shift is imposed, which is more protective than the stated 10 percent threshold.
